search_row.title: Local mate competition sex ratio
search_row.statement: When a few mothers lay eggs on a patch and their offspring mate there before the daughters disperse, the evolutionarily stable sex ratio is female-biased, and the bias weakens as the number of mothers grows.
search_row.math: unbeatable proportion of males x^* = \frac{n-1}{2n} for n foundresses per patch (diploid case)

fields.dct:source: W. D. Hamilton (1967) Extraordinary Sex Ratios
fields.delphi:proposedTest: Vary the number of foundresses per host in a parasitoid wasp (e.g. Nasonia) and compare the offspring sex ratio with (n-1)/(2n).
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: n foundresses per patch, mating confined to the natal patch, only females disperse, mothers control the sex ratio. Formal status: proved as an ESS within the model. Haplodiploidy and inbreeding shift x* slightly.
fields.skos:notation: unbeatable proportion of males x^* = \frac{n-1}{2n} for n foundresses per patch (diploid case)
